# 07. IDs, defaults, updatedAt

## 1) Simple explanation (like I'm 7)
Every row needs a unique ID. Prisma can generate IDs for you (`cuid()`). `@default` sets values automatically. `@updatedAt` automatically changes whenever the row is updated.

## 2) Real name
**Primary keys, defaults, automatic timestamps** — Prisma 7.10.1

## 3) Schema + code example (complete, runnable, commented)
**File:** `prisma-learn/src/07-ids-defaults-updatedat.ts`

```ts
// Chapter 07 — @id, @default, @updatedAt.
// The id is generated by Prisma (cuid) when omitted; updatedAt changes on write.
import { createPrisma } from './lib/prisma.js';

const prisma = createPrisma();

const customer = await prisma.customer.create({
  data: {
    tenantId: 'ten_acme',
    email: 'ch07@acme.test',
    name: 'Chapter Seven',
  },
  select: { id: true, createdAt: true, updatedAt: true },
});
console.log('generated id:', customer.id);

const before = customer.updatedAt;
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
const updated = await prisma.customer.update({
  where: { id: customer.id },
  data: { name: 'Chapter Seven Updated' },
  select: { updatedAt: true },
});
console.log('updatedAt changed:', updated.updatedAt > before, before.toISOString(), '->', updated.updatedAt.toISOString());

await prisma.customer.delete({ where: { id: customer.id } });
await prisma.$disconnect();
```

## 4) The SQL behind it (real `prisma:query` output)
```
prisma:query INSERT INTO "public"."customers" ("id","tenant_id","email","name","display_name","loyalty_points","tier","created_at","updated_at") VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8,$9) RETURNING "public"."customers"."id", "public"."customers"."created_at", "public"."customers"."updated_at" -- params=["clyftjzdk0001xgoh2oo9c2j0","ten_acme","ch07@acme.test","Chapter Seven",null,"0","BRONZE","2026-10-28T05:42:42.044Z","2026-10-28T05:42:42.044Z"]
generated id: clyftjzdk0001xgoh2oo9c2j0
prisma:query UPDATE "public"."customers" SET "name" = $1, "updated_at" = $2 WHERE ("public"."customers"."id") = ($3) AND 1=1 RETURNING "public"."customers"."updated_at" -- params=["Chapter Seven Updated","2026-10-28T05:42:42.072Z","clyftjzdk0001xgoh2oo9c2j0"]
updatedAt changed: true 2026-10-28T05:42:42.044Z -> 2026-10-28T05:42:42.072Z
prisma:query DELETE FROM "public"."customers" WHERE ("public"."customers"."id") = ($1) AND 1=1 RETURNING "public"."customers"."id", "public"."customers"."tenant_id", "public"."customers"."email", "public"."customers"."name", "public"."customers"."display_name", "public"."customers"."phone", "public"."customers"."loyalty_points", "public"."customers"."tier", "public"."customers"."banned_at", "public"."customers"."ban_reason", "public"."customers"."notes", "public"."customers"."deleted_at", "public"."customers"."created_at", "public"."customers"."updated_at" -- params=["clyftjzdk0001xgoh2oo9c2j0"]
```

## 5) What I should see
Prisma generates a `cuid()` when `id` is omitted. `updatedAt` changes on UPDATE. `createdAt` stays the same.

## 6) When to use it / when NOT to
**Use when:** You need automatic ID generation and audit timestamps. Use cuid/uuid for distributed systems, autoincrement for simple sequential IDs.  
**Don't use when:** Exposing sequential integer IDs publicly can be enumerable; consider opaque IDs. Also don't manually set `@updatedAt` values.

## 7) Common mistakes
- Setting `updatedAt` manually (Prisma manages it).
- Using `@default(autoincrement())` without considering scaling/merging.
- Not understanding that `@updatedAt` updates on every `update` call.

## 8) Try it yourself (hint + reset instructions)
**Hint:** Try `@default(uuid())` vs `@default(cuid())` and compare. Update the same row twice and watch `updatedAt`.  
**Reset:** Row is deleted at end of script.
